issues.claim: "Ratings split: 4.6 stars over 429 reviews on Birdeye, 2.5 over 21 on Yelp excerpts, where complaint reviews cite packaging and one an unresolved order."
issues.problem: Minor precision risk, not a factual error: the syndicated excerpt that can be opened (Yahoo Local) shows the long-time customer saying management "refused to make good" and then truncates at "More"; the full Yelp review returns HTTP 403, so the words "unresolved order" are our own reading rather than the visible text. Packaging complaints are directly supported (bag/cardboard-envelope remarks).
issues.fix: Reword to what the excerpt says, e.g. "...cite packaging, and one a customer who says management would not make good on a problem." Keeps the point and is verbatim-safe.

issues.claim: "(... 15–25% absorbed — ... kept below the 34% novice figure from a large software vendor's support desk)"
issues.problem: Framing, not error: the 15–25% band is below the 34% novice figure but above the 14% all-agent average the same paper reports, and NBER 31161 measures a gain in issues resolved per hour, not the share of inquiries an agent can absorb. Citing only the 34% figure makes the estimate look more conservative than it is.
issues.fix: Add "versus 14% average / 34% novice in NBER 31161 (a productivity gain, used here as a loose upper bound)" and, if space allows, say plainly that the band is set by our assumption about absorbed volume, not by the study.

issues.claim: "...and target order errors below 0.5% of shipped orders."
issues.problem: The source states the target as "below 0.5% of shipped orders per quarter". Dropping the period makes the target read as an all-time rate and slightly stricter than published.
issues.fix: Restore the qualifier: "below 0.5% of shipped orders per quarter" (adds three words; see the length note).

issues.claim: Audit body length (title through the "Worth checking together" close, with the disclaimer; excluding the "For the founder" block and Sources)
issues.problem: Approximately 450–460 words by my count, i.e. at or marginally over the ~450-word cap, with no headroom once the fixes above are applied.
issues.fix: Trim ~20–30 words before sending: e.g. shorten the impact-parentheticals ("volume, time and share are our assumption" appears three times) and cut "and certificates" / "for approval" duplication in section 1. Keeping the fixes above then fits under 450.
